file_name: Koumpouros - 2022 - User Centric Design Methodology for mHealth Apps The PainApp Paradigm for Chronic Pain.txt

barriers.description: The evaluation relied on a very small participant sample and a short testing duration, limiting the breadth of user feedback available to the team.
barriers.justification: Small sample size and short testing time constrained the team's ability to evaluate designs and integrate feedback through iterative cycles, hindering 'Evaluate designs' and 'Integrate feedback & iteration' workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Regarding the limitations of the study, we can mention the small size of the population that tested the final application, the short testing time, as well as the absence of a valid and reliable scale for the evaluation of the PainApp.

barriers.description: There was no established, valid, and reliable subjective evaluation scale for mHealth apps in the pain domain, making it difficult to assess app quality.
barriers.justification: The absence of a gold-standard measurement tool directly limited the team's ability to evaluate the design objectively and to integrate validated user-assessment results into iteration and decision-making ('Evaluate designs' and 'Integrate feedback & iteration').
barriers.reference_excerpt: A critical issue that arises from the literature is the lack of a gold standard for the subjective evaluation of mHealth applications. The limited scope of the aforementioned scales makes it hard to find the right tool to assess the quality of an mHealth app targeting the pain domain.

barriers.description: The team developed the first prototype only for Android and restricted field-test participants to Android users, narrowing the user population included in research and testing.
barriers.justification: Limiting platform support and participant eligibility constrained the team's ability to understand diverse user contexts and facilitate broader user involvement, hindering 'Understand context of use' and 'Facilitate user involvement' workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Taking into account the above criteria, we decided to develop the first prototype only in the Android platform. Participants were selected to meet the following criteria: ... (iv) participants must have a smartphone with Android operating system, and (v) should not be the same as the ones involved in the design phase.

barriers.description: Initial requirements gathering requested too much information and there was a risk of technicians unilaterally deciding which data to keep, leading to potential interface complexity.
barriers.justification: Difficulty prioritizing and synthesizing collected information impeded specification of user requirements and producing usable design solutions, affecting 'Specify user requirements' and 'Produce design solutions' workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: For example, too much information was initially requested. The prioritization of information was crucial so as not to lose important data, and at the same time, to preserve all the valuable information for the doctors. A common mistake is either to keep all the originally recorded information or for the technicians to decide what should be kept or not. This greatly affects the graphical user interface, making it usually very complex, resulting in the final application losing its value.
